_note: Configuration presets consumed by scripts/auto-populate-configuration.py. Each preset declares the parameters of the floor + cost-ceiling + cost-sort algorithm. Floor values are percentages of the top intelligence score within a bucket. Cost ceilings are $/M blended tokens. Optimum can derive an adaptive ceiling from the current high-end normal price while trimming obvious price outliers. The 'mode' field switches the algorithm path: 'paid_intelligence' (Premium/Optimum/Budget) operates over paid models; 'free_intelligence' operates over the free models list with no cost math.

premium.description: Highest-ranking models available; cost ignored. Best-of-bucket per slot.

optimum.description: Cheapest models that pass a moving quality floor and adaptive price ceiling. Most users land here.

adaptive_cost_ceiling._note: Start Optimum at 30% of the current high-end normal price. The peak ignores prices above 3x the median of floor-qualified candidates so GPT-Pro/o1-style outliers do not anchor value picks.

budget.description: Best models below the matching Optimum price band. The ceiling starts one cent below the cheapest Optimum pick in that lane; quality loosens downward until enough models pass.

reference_cost_ceiling._note: Budget stays just below Optimum's cheapest matching lane. If the first pass is too strict, the quality floor drops before the ceiling widens.

free.description: Free-tier models only. Intelligence-descending. Free Models Router included as the first option when available.

speed.description: Fastest first response. Ranks every slot by lowest time-to-first-token (then throughput) within an intelligence floor and a cost ceiling; reasoning models excluded (they stall before the first token). Latency from OpenRouter per-provider stats (or_ttft_ms), AA median (latency_ttft_seconds) as fallback.
speed._note: PROVISIONAL tuning constants pending empirical calibration: floor_pct 40 / min_floor_pct 25 (intelligence floor) and adaptive_cost_ceiling.peak_fraction 0.4 (cost ceiling) are first-pass picks, not measured optima — retune once Speed bakes can be observed against real registry latency data. The latency_asc sort + reasoning exclusion are applied UNIFORMLY to every slot (big1/big2/fast/small) by populate_configuration's speed_mode path, overriding any slot-level sort_by.

utility._note: top_n=3 feeds the popout's three-row small section (1 primary + 2 fallbacks).

analysis.gear4._note: When diversity is enforced for the workhorse pair, breadth picks exclude depth's primary so the second slot reaches for a different model family. top_n=4 feeds the popout's four-row large section (1 primary + 3 fallbacks per chain).

analysis.gear3._note: Retained for backward compatibility. The Fast slot owns gear3.depth + gear3.breadth in the new schema (2026-05-23) — populate_configuration skips this block when slot_specs.fast is present.

fast._note: Mid-tier speed-optimized slot. Primary → gear3.depth + utility.gear2_rag_lookup; secondary → gear3.breadth when adversarial diversity is on (mirrored from primary via post-bake when off). Fast is vision_required so the visual pane always has a fast vision model available even when the global Vision-only toggle is off. No size_bucket gate. min_tokens_per_second=80 is a hard floor, and models with no throughput data do not pass. After that speed gate, each preset optimizes normally: Premium by intelligence, Optimum/Budget by their value/cost rules. floor_pct=30 for COST-first presets keeps the fast slot from inheriting a quality bar that prices out cheap fast models. floor_pct_if_intelligence_first=80 for Premium keeps its fast slot high-intelligence among fast-enough models. top_n=4 → 1 primary + 3 fallbacks per chain, mirror of analysis.gear4.

vision_substitute._note: Vision substitute picks come from the large bucket filtered to vision_capable=True. Threaded into every cell's vision_substitute field.
